topic: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana

subtopics.title: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana scheme
subtopics.summary: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana is a rooftop solar scheme launched in 2024 and described as the world's largest domestic rooftop solar initiative. Its aim is to provide free electricity up to 300 units to households by installing rooftop solar panels. The scheme offers a subsidy of up to 40% on panel installation and targets 1 crore households by 2027, with the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy as nodal ministry. A parallel Model Solar Village initiative asks each district to establish one such village to promote energy self-reliance.
facts: Launched in 2024
World's largest domestic rooftop solar initiative
Aim: free electricity up to 300 units per household
Subsidy of up to 40% for rooftop solar panel installation
Target: rooftop solar in 1 crore households by 2027
Nodal ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
World Bank approved USD 890 million to support the programme
Model Solar Village: one per district to promote energy self-reliance
Model Solar Village eligibility: population above 5,000 (2,000 in special category states)
Top contributing states: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan

subtopics.title: International Solar Alliance (ISA)
subtopics.summary: The International Solar Alliance (ISA) is a treaty-based intergovernmental organisation of solar-rich countries lying between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn. It was launched jointly by India and France in 2015 during COP21 in Paris. Its membership comprises 112 members and 15 signatory countries, and its headquarters is in Gurugram.
facts: Launched jointly by India and France in 2015 during COP21 (Paris)

Headquarters: Gurugram (National Institute for Solar Energy of India)
Mission: mobilise USD 1 trillion in solar investments by 2030
Mission: install 1,000 GW of solar capacity

subtopics.title: India's solar position and records
subtopics.summary: According to IRENA Renewable Energy Statistics 2026, India added 37 GW of solar capacity in 2025 and became the world's second largest solar growth market. India overtook Japan to become the world's third largest solar power producer in 2025. The country also hosts Bhadla Solar Park, India's largest solar plant at 2245 MW, and Omkareshwar, India's largest floating solar plant at 600 MW.

subtopics.title: Global initiatives and climate commitments
subtopics.summary: India's COP26 climate commitments, called Panchamrita, include net zero by 2070 and 500 GW of non-fossil energy capacity by 2030. The Global Solar Facility, launched at COP27 in 2022, provides payment guarantees to de-risk solar investments. The OSOWOG concept, first proposed by India in 2018, advocates trans-national solar power connectivity through integrated regional grids.

quizzes.passage: The International Solar Alliance is an international body set up to promote solar energy across the world. It is aimed at solar-rich countries that lie between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn, and it is described as a treaty-based intergovernmental organisation. The alliance states its aim as ensuring clean, reliable and affordable access to solar energy, which it links to sustainable growth and an improved quality of life. Its vision is a short phrase that asks members to work together to make the sun brighter. Membership rules have also widened over time. Countries from outside the tropics are allowed to join, although they are excluded from voting rights. Recognition from the wider United Nations system has also followed over the years. This makes the alliance a platform for solar-rich nations to coordinate their efforts. The alliance's mission goes beyond membership. It aims to provide clean energy access to a very large population and to mitigate solar-related emissions across the globe. It also seeks to promote low-cost, sustainable and equitable solar systems in the least developed countries and small island developing states. Together, these features give the alliance a clear geographic base, an inclusive membership and a practical focus on people who need energy access.

quizzes.passage: Many families spend a steady share of their income on electricity, and a rooftop solar programme offers one way to reduce that cost. The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana is built around this idea. It encourages households to install solar panels on their rooftops so that the home can draw power from the sun. The scheme is described as the largest programme of its kind in the world, which reflects how many homes it is meant to reach. Because panels can be costly for ordinary families, the government offers financial support in the form of a subsidy that lowers the share of cost paid by each household. The basic goal is to give households free electricity up to a set number of units. The programme has also drawn outside finance. An international development bank has approved funds to support India's rooftop solar programme, which shows that the effort has attracted attention beyond the country. Alongside the household scheme, the government promotes a model solar village idea. Under this idea, villages are encouraged to become self-reliant in energy. Eligibility depends on population size, and special category states follow a lower threshold. Taken together, these measures link clean energy with everyday household life and with village-level independence. Such schemes also show how energy policy can reach households directly.
